column6: Any of a number of Console Software errors. This error could also indicate that a software upgrade was recently performed.
Either the Stop buton was pressed by the user, or an AU error caused the interuption of a run.
The Instrument software could not complete an operation in a timely fashion.

This error is posted normally after an error which results in all in-progress tests to be aborted. The AU has found vessels it will abortpast the substrate dispense probe. There is no trouble shooting required for this message.
At some point in the middle of a sample probe or substrate probe drawback operation, this operation was interupted. When this occurs, the instrument cannot run until a prime all has been performed.
The wash wheel software will report this error if it scheduled to perform a move, but it detects that either the dispense or aspirate plate are currently retarcted.
AU was initialized.
While running the Restore Utility, the user selected to delete unloaded packs from the database.
Calibration failed for the displayed assay.
This error is posted if a QC results is posted that is either out of range, or was resported with fatal flags.
Calibration passed.
This event is posted upon successful completion of running the Reagent Pipettor Matching routine.
Reagent pipettor matching was run and the new Pump correction Factors were accepted by the user.
User has enabled the Utilit Routine.
User has disabled the Ulility Routine.

Event log message indicating that the instrument just trasitioned to Unknown Mode. Unknown Mode is when communications have been disrupted between the Console and the AU. This could be because the AU software crashed, power was lost to the AU, or the network connection between the Console and the AU was lost.
Instrument transitioned to not ready mode, either through a fatal hardware or software error or by the user pressing the stop button.
Instrument transitioned to pause mode, either through a device error or by the user pressing the pause button.
Event log message indicating that the instrument just transitioned to Run Mode.
The user has pressed the Stop Button.
The customer has pressed the pause mode making the instrument transition to Pause Mode.
Resume button was pressed by the user.
Event log message indicating that the instrument just transitioned to Ready Mode.
The console Recovery Option successfully recovered a disabled subsystem.
An error occured with the low level communications between the Console PC and the Instrument AU.
Unspecified communication error occured.
The user changed the test units for one of the assays.
This event is posted when data is received from the LIS in an incorrect format.
AU software may have crashed, AU may have been shutdown or the network connection between the AU and the Console was lost.
This error is posted when some part of the Console UI software crashes.
The hospital LIS system sent a test request without the test number identified in the LIS request.

LIS received a test request for a sample ID already in receieved by the Console with a different Patient ID. The LIS software does not allow changing a Patient ID after receiving the first LIS request.
LIS host connection was done for some reason.

This message is posted if one of the Console programs crashes, and a running Console program tries to talk to the crashed program. This message should be posted in conjunction with other Console related error messages associated with a Console UI crash to the Windows NT desktop.
An auto alignment operation failed.
During priming, an unspecified device failed.

Rack exited with no tests ordered. This could be because the user loaded a rack with no ordered samples, or the LIS query was performed and no tests were found for the bar coded samples. Check the LIS timeout just in case the Console released the rack before the LIS could send its test orders.
An Alignment has changed.
This message is posted after a Pipettor Matching is accepted and indicates the need to perform pipettor matching.
The Wash Buffer bubble detection hardware reported excessive bubbles in the line.
this Event log message indicates that an APF has been loaded and the indicated assay has been updated.
Somehow the instrument decremented below zero for a particular substrate bottle.
Warning message that onboard substrate is about to expire.
Warning message that the indicated pack is about to expire.
Warning message indicating that the lot will expire in three days.
Warning that the curve for the displayed assay and Lot # is about to expire.
Thie event is reported after successfully performing a Console Database restore using the Restore Utility application.
Console software was launched either through a reboot of the Console PC, or was launched from the Windows NT Desktop.
User has changed the system time on the Console PC.
Message displayed when the database management service runs. This service deletes old data and keeps your database small and fast.
Message displayed when the database management service runs. This service deletes old data and keeps your database small and fast.
Auto delete settings were changed.
A bad formatted LIS message was received by the LIS software on the Console PC.
Some database error occured. Need to look in the details for more specific information.
This event is posted if the Console database software detects an error while performing a query. Queries are performed when using the test results filter in the Test Results screen.
During barcoding an expired substrate was attempted to be loaded.
Either a reagent pack was loaded that was expired, or a remap was perfomed with expired packs. Packs will show up with ??? in the Reagent Storage screen.

A pack was loaded that had been previously deleted either by the user deleting the pack from the Reagent Invetory screen, or in the process of recovering from a Critical Event jam were packs opened packs were not loaded on the instrument.
Somehow a missmatch was created between the Console and the Instrument substrate counts. This could have been created as a result of deleted critical events.
The user took too long to bar code the substrate so this message was posted to the Event Log.
The AU threw away a sample vessel that could not start running within three hours. This could be due to AU errors that interrupted test or Supply Wait conditions.

The Console software sent sampletube information to the Instrument for a sampletube no longer present in the SPU. This error can occur when sampletubes are unloaded from the Instrument at a time when the Console UI software may not be running, or vice versa.
This event is posted if the Console receives a message from the Instrument for a test result, sample vessel, or reagent pack that the Console does not know about.
A message from the Instrument to the Console PC was sent but could not be properly processed by the Console software. This could have resulted in a critical event jam.
Reagent Pipettor has been disabled either by error, or by the user.
Pipettor has become enabled.
The instrument has run out of a supply and can no longer start scheduling tests to run.

A bar coded sample tube was placed in a rack in a position that had already been programmed manually. The barcode of the sample tube was read and it did not match the Sample ID that was manually entered. The manual entered Sample ID was then used instead of the bar code.

An instrument condition or configuration caused the DxI status to change from OK to Not OK. This occurs when any one of 10 subsystems change states from a '1' to a '0' as shown in the event's details. In Dynamic LAS mode, tubes will not sort to a DxI with a 'Not OK' status.

An instrument condition or configuration caused the DxI status to change from Not OK to OK. This occurs when any one of 10 subsystems change states from a '0' to a '1' as shown in the event's details.
There has been some error associated with printing of reports.
This event is posted if the PnP sensor is in a wrong position. Launch the AU software using pcAnywere and choose WAIT when the Machine Control Window is displayed. Choose Touch-And-Toss option.
The Bulk Feeder experienced an error with the lower ejector.
The Bulk Feeder lower ejector jammed.

Binding of scoops, Jammed vessel between hopper and scoop, Ejector piston not fully retracted before scoop moves, Misalignment of pistons to scoops, Mechanical problems with the elevator assembly, Electrical connections.

The Sample PnP device went to go and pick up an RV and/or a DV and no vessel was felt in the RV Supply Carriage or the Sample PnP went to put down an RV or DV and the vessel was not felt. For the first case this could be due to the Bulk Feeder not adequately keeping up with the RV demands of the system (so-called vessel starving).

This event can be posted if a sample vessel cannot be delivered in time to start a test. This normally is due to the bulk feeder not being able to keep up with the test demands and requires no servicing.
Most likeley the PnP could not feel the vessel when it tried to put the vessel into its destination.

The PnP tried to deliver a vessel, and when it put the vessel down it could not feel that the vessel was delivered. This could be because the PnP never picked up the vessel in the first place, or it could be that a shuttle that was to receive the vessel was not in its correct position and the PnP dropped the vessel onto the baseplate.

A PnP went to pick up a vessel, or verify that a vessel was present but did not detect the vessel by looking at the ejector piston sensor status. The vessel could be missing, or the vessel could be present but there is a failure of the ejector piston sensor.  Check ribbon cable.

When attempting to place a vessel into the Wash Wheel either by the IncubatepnP or the WashPnP, the software detected that a vessel was already in this position. No mechanical check was made, only a check with the software. If you see this event, please send to Chaska Technical support the TRACE file containing this error.
A PnP detected the presence of a vessel that should not have been detected. This could be due to a failed vessel transfer or an issue with the ejector hall effect sensor.
Interlock switches detected either the left or righ cover was opened.
This event is posted if the instrument detects that the Reagent Storage door has been opened. Perform a remap function to recover.
User was requested to remove racks and this was not done.
Something blocked the putting down of a vessel by the PnP. This could be a stranded vessel, or it could be a shuttle that was not in the correct position to receive a vessel.
Non-specified device could not find its home sensor.
Instrument failed to initialize due to some hardware issue. See individual occurances for hints as to why initialization failed.

During running of either the Daily or Special Clean, an error caused the operation to fail. When this happens, it is required that a full initialization be performed due to the possibility of RVs left in the Sample and or Wash Wheel.
Sample or Reagent Pipettor has been disabled either by error, or by the user.
A pipettor became disabled, and the user is trying to re-enable that pipettor. A pipettor cannot be enabled until an initialization has been done first.
During a clean out of the Wash Wheel, a fatal error occured. The Instrument will retry the operation.

An attempt to return a SV to the sample wheel could not be completed due to the possible presence of a RV and/or DV in the PnP. The PnP cannot physically enter the wheel holding either of these vessels.
The aspirate plate within the wash arm assembly experienced a fatal movement error.
Dispense arm was unable to complete its move.
Wash wheel failed to home.
Excessive motor slippage was detcted for the Wash Wheel.
The wash wheel moved a slot during a dark read.
Pressure seen during aspiration of Aspirate Probe #1 exceeded the allowable limits.
The ejector plate sensor did not detect that the ejector plate was extended. Could be a physical jam or a faulty sensor.
Wash collar vacuum for aspirate probe #1 was less than 100. Could be torn duckbill, or compromised vacuum subsystem.
Sensor within the Bulk Feeder was not obstructed so the feeder thinks it has less than 1000 vessels. As vessels move within the Hopper, this message and the RV Supply refilled message can be posted.
Temperature now is back in specifications and the system is ready to start processing samples.
At least one critical temperature is out of specification and the system is waiting until that temperature stabilizes before allowing any tests to start processing.
The aspirate probe plate motor slipped, most likely due to a mechanical obstruction of the aspirate probe plate.

There was an inconsistency found between what the software thinks the aspirate pump is doing and what the status of the motor is. The software might think the pump is moving, when the hardware status returned from the pump says that the pump is idle.

During cleanup of the wash wheel a vessel was found that was not by the software supposed to be in the wheel. This is most likely due to a missed toss  of a vessel fro the Wash Wheel to the solid waste,

During the check of the wash collar vacuum, when an empty vessel was under the #1 aspirate probe, the vacuum was below the limits of 1000. This could be due to a known issue with the instrument when measuring the wash collar vacuums when no vessel is present, or it could indicate an isse with the duck bill or vacuum system. Look for Wash Collar vacuum errors to confirm issues with the duckbill or vacuum subsystem.

This error can occur if no RV is present in the Supply Carriage at the time the Sample PnP attempts to grab an empty SV to place into the Sample Wheel. This may be due to the Bulk Feeder not being able to keep up with the demands of the instrument.

During level detect of the sample vessel, the reagent pipettor detected fluid, but not at the height it expected. This is predominately due to incorrect sample containers being used on designated racks, but it can also be due to sample dispense errors, sample foaming or other pump related issues.
Customer has loaded too many tests to run.
A bad sample tube bar code was attempted to be read.
Onloader pusher movement was obstructed.
There has been a failure of the SPU off loader, the area of the SPU were racks are moved to after being sampled.
Presentation Tray is most likely jammed.
Customer was requested to remove racks from the SPU either for STAT loading or for clearing a SPU jam.
User loaded a backwards rack.
Warning message displayed to the user when the SPU loader cover has been left open for too long of a time (2 minutes).
The rack at end sensor has failed.
Informational Event Log message reminding the user to close the offload cover.
The SPU bar code reader attempted to read a bar code with illegal characters.
This event is posted if the customer loads a rack that is currently not specified with a sampletube type within the Rack ID Setup Screen.
Offload are is jammed.
Informational message to tell the user that they need to empty the SPU of all racks. Usually follows a SPU jam or other rack loading error.
The Presentation Unit sensor has failed and is no longer detecting the presence of racks.
SPU needs to be initialized, but LAS is available to deliver sample tubes.
This error is posted if the customer attempts to load a rack while either the Daily or Special Clean routines are running.

SPU error that get's posted under various conditions that says that there has been a motor failure, when in fact no motor failure has actually occured. The error can be posted simply due to the front Covers being opened and there was power loss to the SPU subsystem. It can also get posted if an error is generated while downloading the BarCode parameters to the bar code reader. To recover, you are required to initialize the SPU.

Now [No RV found in the Supply Carriage]. The Sample PnP went to pick up a vessel from the supply carriage and no vessel was found. This is most likely due to the Bulk Feeder unable to keep up with the RV supply demand.

This error is posted usually for the case that one of the reagent shuttle carriages becomes disabled, though a device error, but the Reagent Pipettor subsystem does not know yet that the reagent shuttle has been disabled. There is no trouble shooting associated with this event.
A high sample caused Dark Counts to exceed their limits.
A very high RLU sample was read by the Analytical Module luminometer. This could be a very high sample or could indicate a spill on the Wash Wheel.
Crosstalk exceeded allowable RLU limits. Check wheel for spillage.
Air Compressor failure
Low compressor pressure. Trouble shoot compressor, look for leaks.

Process moitoring either detected too high of a vacuum for the sample wash tower indicating a possible obstruction, or two low indicating an issues with teh vacuum associated with the sample wash tower.

Process moitoring either detected too high of a vacuum for the reagent wash tower indicating a possible obstruction, or too low indicating an issues with the vacuum associated with the reagent wash tower.

Non-reported device error occured. This error is normally followed by a more specific error. Terse file data has insufficient information to characterize this error. [FluidLevelControl=Wash Buffer Supply, Motor Controller=Transfer Pump]
Speed of the mixer motor was too slow.
An unspecified device had a motion error.

This error will be posted if sudden unexpected power loss is experienced by the AU. opening the covers without the interlocks cheated will result in this error message if the cover is open during operation of the AU.
A motor experienced excessive slippage.
An unspecified device had a motion error in the X Axis.
An unspecified device's z-home sensor was found in an unexpected position possibly indicating the device experienced excessive slippage.
An unspecified device experienced a z-axis motion error.

During the dispense of sample or reagents, process monitoring detetected either a pressure area greater than limits indicating a possible obstruction, or under limits indicating the possibility of short sampling.
Liquid waste is full.

When the Reagent Pipettor went to level sense inside the Sample Vessel in preperation to start running a test, the Reagent Pipettor detected the fluid surface, but by calculation did not sense enough sample volume to run the test. The Test assosciated was aborted and had the QNS flag applied.
Pump piston failed to home. Pump could be frozen or sticky.
An unspecified pump had a motion failure.
Pump piston slippage error.
This event is posted under numerous conditions indicating that the pipettor failed to be washed.
Bubbles were detected in the substrate line through the Process Monitoring hardware and software.
Substrate bubble detect process monitoring has failed thee consecutive times. As a result the instrument was forced into Internal Pause Mode.
Susbtrate pump failed to home.
An unspecified pump valve failed to home.
Excessive slippage was detected in one of the pump valves.
Slippage was detected on Wash Pump #1.
Wash pump valve failed to home. This error could be due to a mechanical issue, but could also be due to the user not performing a complete initialization of the instrument after leaving Diagnostics.
Wash Pump #2 piston did not home properly.
Wash pump valve failed to home. This error could be due to a mechanical issue, but could also be due to the user not performing a complete initialization of the instrument after leaving Diagnostics.
Not enough sample was detected in the primary sample tube.
Instrument has run out of Wash Buffer as is seen by the Wash Buffer weight sensors.
Warning that the Wash Buffer supply is low.
This message is normally posted when one bottle becomes full on the system leaving only one bottle left for the liquid waste.
Solid waste is within 204564214f being full.
When attempting to level sense the primary sample tube, enough sample volume was found to run the requested tests, but not enough sample volume was found to take the additional reserve sample volume.

During the washing of the probe, not enough pressure was seen by peri-flow Process Monitoring. This could be due to failed sensor or inadequate wash buffer being delivered to the wash tower either due to a failed pump, or obstruction of the lines.
The peri-flow process monitoring did not detect wash buffer delivery into the Wash Tower.

The buffer supply line is monitored for air (empty cubitainer or damaged tubing) and occlusion (excessive restriction). The air sensor is sampled at 40Hz and the occlusion at 8Hz. The acquisition window is nominally one second in length, with a maximum duration of 1.1 seconds. If less than 40 samples were acquired in this time, excessive CPU load was probably to blame and an informational error is reported. Error handling is done if any air or ocllusion fault(s) are detected.
Sample process was disabled due to too many consecutive peri-flow errors.
This error is posted by the Sample Pipettor RF Level Sense hardware when the VCO cannot get running.
This is some kind of low level device error associated with the electronics. This error can be seen as a result of the covers being opened during operation of the AU.
In most cases this error is seen in conjunction with an Idle timer expired error". However

Either SUBSYSTEM.INI, SMC.INI or XXX were modified after software installation. You can eliminate this error by copying these files located in C:\AU to the C:\AU\Default directory.

During initialization a check is made if any process monitoring has been disabled though changes to the SPECIFIC.INI file. This message is posted if any process monitoring systems have been disabled. [enabled = no].
Due to a fatal error, a subsystem was disabled.
This event can be posted by a functioning subsystem that has timed out waiting for a disabled subsytem.
An obstruction was detected during aspiration of either the Sample Probe or one of the Reagent Probes.
A subsystem did not complete an operation within the expected time.
An unspecified device failed to home in the X-Axis direction.
An unspecified device failed to home in the z-axis.

The backlash of the substrate pump is too large. Backlash is the amount of looseness of the belt. The current threshold for generating this error is 220 steps. Backlash is checked periodically while the instrument is running.
Wash buffer confirmation failed to detect fluid during wash buffer dispensing.
The Wash Wheel encoder detected the location of the wash wheel outside of expected limits.
Indicates some issue with electronics and the MCC board. Could be related to unexpected power loss due to opening either the left or right instrument covers.
Slippage occured while attempting to home an unspecified device.
The substrate pump backlash limit of 220 was exceeded. Correct by inspecting and cleaning the substrate pump and belt.
Vessel did not eject properly from the PnP.
There was a barcode reader error when trying to read the pack in loader position #1
Bar code reader in teh Reagent Loda Tray failed to properly read a pack barcode.
There was a barcode reader error when trying to read the pack in loader position #1
The bar code reader failed to read the pack bar code.
Reagent Storage Tray was jammed.
Customer has attempted to load to many reagent packs.

Sometimes the reagent subsystem cannot get a pack into teh pipetting position fast enough. When this happens, this event log message is posted. Unless this is happing at a high frequency it is not a message that is of concern. No tests are lost, and the test is rescheduled."
The gripper sensor did not detect that the gripper was open after handling a pack.
Gripper had problems grabbing a pack. Look for broken couplers, sensor issues with the gripper or rough movement of the gripper in the x or Y direction.
Reagent Storage temperature is too high andmay compromise the pack integrity.
Reagent Supply interlock switch thinks the door is open.
Reagent Supply interlock switch thinks the door is open.

The Reagent Storage Module interface PCB has lost its memory. Proceed to the 'Resetting the Reagent Gripper Encoders' section. Note: Loss of memory is normal if the instrument has been powered off for several days.

Something is obstructing the closing of the reagent storage waste door. This could be an issues with the sensor, or something mechanically obstructing the door like a loose pack. Issues with the air compressos may also cause this eent to be posted.
Warning to the user that the solid waste door has been left open. RVs will not be discarded if the solid waste door is open.
During the utility routine the gripper is opened and closes and the amount of time this takes is checked, The gripper took longer tham expected to open and close during this check.
A general ultrasonics error has occured.
Error posted when the Reagent pipettor could not detect sample within the Sample Vessel, or some other error occured within the ultrasonics subsystem.

When the customer attempts to load a new substrate bottle, a timout can occur if the customer does not close th substrate door in a specified time. This event is posted if this time limit is exceeded.
The LAS Connector Unit not connected. Verify LAS is operational.

This message is generated when a tube arrives at the query bar code reader (BR03) and is not released into the hardware queue. Some other error has occurred and the tubes scanned at the aspiration barcode reader (BR02) do not match the tubes in the software queue.  Until the hardware queue is empty, no new tubes will be released from the query bar code reader (BR03). Once the hardware and software queues are empty, the Connection Unit will begin releasing tubes into the hardware queue from BR03.  These samples will be aspirated if no other errors occur.

This message is not associated with pressing the Pause button on the DxI connection unit keypad. This message is generated when the DxI connector unit encounters an error when the Get Tube or Release Tube message was issued.  When a valid response is received, normal operation is resumed.  Typically, no customer intervention is required.

DxI allowed hardware reset queue operation to continue (mode 84). All the tubes are removed from the software queue of the DxI. These tubes will be in the Work Pending list on the DxI.  PrepLink considers these samples complete and they will be sent to the Stockyard.  These samples must be processed manually.
DxI denied reset queue request from the DxI connection unit due to current system conditions.

The tube at the aspiration bar code reader is not in the software queue.  The system will release the tube without aspirating sample.This message is most likely to occur when a sample carrier that is stuck in the hardware queue is released.  When this sample carrier reaches the aspiration barcode reader, the sample ID is no longer in the software queue.PrepLink will consider this sample complete and the sample ID will appear in the DxI Work Pending list.  This sample must be processed manually.
Samle barcode could not be verified.

The aspiration was scheduled for a particular tube but the DxI did not receive the sample ID from the aspiration barcode reader (BR02) by the time the Sample Pipettor was at the aspiration point. This condition could be caused by: 1) PLC taking too long to read the barcode. 2) Connector Unit paused. 3) Communication error.  The tube that caused the error may be released and sample may not be aspirated.  The sample ID will be in the Work Pending List.  The tube will be in the Stockyard and PrepLink considers this tube complete

A sample tube was routed to the instrument, but it was released without any aliquot taken because no test request was received within the LIS timeout period. This could be because the LIS was temporarily off-line, or the test request was received too late. If this error is occuring freqently, check the LIS timeout period set with the LIS setup screen.

The tube was removed from the queue as a result of Reset Queue. All tests go to Work Pending on DxI.  PrepLink will think the samples are complete.  Samples will have to be manually loaded on the DxI.

A tube that was accepted into the Queue was not seen at the Aspiration BCR before the Queue was declared empty by the Connection Unit. DxI keeps track of Sample IDs in a 'software queue' as they are added at the Query BCR and subtracted when released from the Aspiration BCR

This message is not associated with pressing the Pause button on the DxI connection unit keypad. This message is generated when the DxI connector unit encounters an error when the Get Tube or Release Tube message was issued.  When a valid response is received, normal operation is resumed.  Typically, no customer intervention is required.

The current state of Sample Pipettor is preventing sample aspiration.  The Sample Pipettor cannot more or isn't moving.  A corresponding sample pipettor error or other error which prevents the pipettor from moving should be in the DxI event log.  No error will be generated on the DxI Connection unit.
Console has successfully communicated with the Power Processor unit.
